cues.note: selection rings, planet owner rings and ownership markers decided by the game; marker pixel size is derived from this window's camera so the icon stays 9-15 px at any zoom; lines are one pixel wide because bgfx has no line width

emissive.blend: additive, no depth write; bolts sized in pixels at this camera

fog.blend: alpha, depth test off (the mask covers unexplored space, not geometry)
fog.note: the mask is Python's classification, one texel per visibility cell; the window samples it and decides nothing about visibility

hardware.note: surface hardware crosses as a full basis (FLAG_SURFACE_FRAME) that the window copies verbatim, because a building stands on the foundation the site generator chose; its mesh arrives on the mesh ring because the offline catalogue cannot name a building that is constructed during a match; role colours are the shared palette, not on the wire

hits.blend: alpha, no depth test, no depth write
hits.note: rebuilt from position, normal, size, age and seed like a blast; the seeded spark fragments come from this window's port of Python's random.Random, so a seed produces the same flecks on both sides

live.note: Producer-only frames: no simulation or HUD is drawn by this window. frames_behind counts producer frames published while this frame was being drawn; it is not wall-clock latency and not a frame rate.

assumptions: Four human slots, same Imperial faction, distinct colours, hostile teams; no strategic AI.
Direct factory setup of completed hardware, colonies and staggered convoys; not a replay of paid construction, resource gathering, colonization or station-site validation; no build queues.

Requested pre-existing fleet exceeds current stock construction command capacity (906 used / 78 available per player); no capacity rules changed. This is a scale workload, not a proof this exact economy can build the fleet.

Ten ordinary stations include the command station; two eligible colonies supply stock command capacity. Infrastructure sites are prebuilt, not proof of an organic build history (mines/relay require suitable terrain when constructed).
Four extra trade stations per player; four pre-existing convoys per source, nearest own market.
Convoys start at staggered route progress; deliveries remove hulls normally, never respawned by fixture.
At most 300 fixed 30 Hz ticks (10 simulated seconds), below the stock 45s convoy spawn interval.
Player 0 live fog/sensors, not an omniscient all-map graphics load; visibility reported per sample.
Close inspection uses the distributed world with a fixed flagship camera; not all assets are on screen.
Versioned class mix is a benchmark assumption, not an approved gameplay distribution.
Combat is an established interleaved four-way melee, held stock hulls with automatic targeting; no forced damage or godmode.
Omniscient diagnostic export; not ordinary player visibility.
Artificial catalogue grid, synthetic IDs/transforms; checksum refers to unchanged source fixture, not this layout.
metadata.checksum: game.benchmark.state_hash: full precise state before and after extraction
metadata.name: four-player-combat-v1
metadata.profile: W00/W01 offline JSON; not W02 shared memory or a throughput claim
metadata.scale_policy: Inspection grid: raw authored mesh units, scale 1; not gameplay size.

planets.note: one blob per distinct planet, published once; the body is a unit sphere scaled by the frame instance's radius, spun at 1.2 rad/s like the Python renderer

shields.note: one instanced camera-facing hemisphere per shielded unit, alpha baked from latitude like renderer.py::_shield_shell_list; tint and fade are Python's strength ramp, the detail level and the readability floor come from this camera

timing_scope: Unsynchronized offline mesh-only frame loop; excludes simulation, HUD, fog, effects, LAN; capture can affect timing
